form.label: AI Discovery Runtime Planes
form.description: What actually ran, beside AI Discovery's inventory of what is present. Coverage is the first row on purpose: findings from a blinded host must not be read as a clean result.

html.p: Any non-zero value means findings from this host are incomplete. A detector reporting clean because it was never able to look is indistinguishable, on a dashboard, from a host that is genuinely clean.

search.query: `defenseclaw_demo_ai_runtime_events` | where event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" AND runtime_plane_running IN ("false","False",0) | stats dc(runtime_plane) as planes_down

html.p: On an unprivileged POSIX host this is how much of the machine's egress cannot be named — the difference between a quiet host and a blind sensor. Windows reports the owning pid in every row, so a non-zero value there means something else.

search.query: `defenseclaw_demo_ai_runtime_events` | where event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" | stats max(runtime_connections_unattributed) as unattributed

html.p: A degraded poll is never reported as a complete one, so this counts exactly the cycles whose findings must be read as incomplete.

search.query: `defenseclaw_demo_ai_runtime_events` | where event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" AND outcome="partial" | stats count as partial_cycles

panel.title: Plane health — every plane, every cycle

search.query: `defenseclaw_demo_ai_runtime_events` | where event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" | stats latest(runtime_plane_available) as available, latest(runtime_plane_running) as running, latest(runtime_plane_backend) as source, latest(runtime_plane_mechanism) as mechanism, latest(runtime_events_lost) as events_lost, latest(runtime_loss_known) as loss_known, latest(runtime_container_events) as container_events, latest(runtime_plane_reason) as reason, latest(_time) as last_seen by host, runtime_plane | eval events_lost=case(isnull(events_lost), "", loss_known="false", events_lost." (stream drops only)", 1=1, events_lost) | fields - loss_known | eval last_seen=strftime(last_seen, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") | rename runtime_plane as plane | sort host plane

html.p: The latest plane c record of each host: the Tetragon version, the Plane C backend, the enterprise.tetragon mode, the approval of the build's kernel controls, how many enrolled users enforce or are still in burn-in, the pause and the control-set digest. A host on the native backend with Tetragon installed enforces nothing.

search.query: `defenseclaw_demo_ai_runtime_events` | where event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" AND runtime_plane="c" AND runtime_kernel_helper_mode!="" | stats latest(runtime_tetragon_version) as tetragon, latest(runtime_plane_backend) as backend, latest(runtime_kernel_helper_mode) as mode, latest(runtime_kernel_approval) as approval, latest(runtime_kernel_users_enforced) as enforcing, latest(runtime_kernel_users_enrolled) as enrolled, latest(runtime_kernel_users_burn_in) as "in burn-in", latest(runtime_kernel_paused) as paused, latest(runtime_policy_version) as digest, sum(runtime_kernel_blocked_delta) as denials, sum(runtime_kernel_would_block_delta) as "would-block", latest(_time) as last_seen by host | eval last_seen=strftime(last_seen, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") | sort host

`defenseclaw_demo_ai_runtime_events` | where event_name="ai.runtime.finding" AND ($severity|s$="*" OR runtime_severity=$severity|s$) AND ($agent|s$="*" OR runtime_agent=$agent|s$) | timechart span=10m count by runtime_severity

html.p: unaccounted is the interesting reading: a complete discovery scan that explains none of what the runtime planes are watching. unobserved means there was no usable inventory, and the score was left untouched in both directions.

search.query: `defenseclaw_demo_ai_runtime_events` | where event_name="ai.runtime.finding" | stats count by runtime_verdict

`defenseclaw_demo_ai_runtime_events` | where event_name="ai.runtime.finding" AND ($severity|s$="*" OR runtime_severity=$severity|s$) AND ($agent|s$="*" OR runtime_agent=$agent|s$) | table _time, runtime_severity, runtime_score, runtime_process, runtime_agent, runtime_verdict, runtime_reason, runtime_finding_id | rename runtime_severity as severity, runtime_score as score, runtime_process as process, runtime_agent as agent, runtime_verdict as inventory, runtime_reason as "inventory reason", runtime_finding_id as finding | sort - score

html.p: Every tactic here is gated on an AI agent appearing in the process lineage: a developer running sudo produces nothing, the same sudo under an agent produces a signal. This row renders empty unless the host plane is enabled, which is worth knowing before reading an empty row as a clean host.

search.query: `defenseclaw_demo_ai_runtime_events` | where event_name="ai.runtime.activity" AND ($agent|s$="*" OR runtime_agent=$agent|s$) | timechart span=10m count by runtime_tactic

panel.title: Agent activity — one record per tactic

html.p: The sequence is the finding: reading a credential is a lead, and reading a credential then minting an identity then uploading to a paste site is an incident.

search.query: `defenseclaw_demo_ai_runtime_events` | where event_name="ai.runtime.activity" AND ($agent|s$="*" OR runtime_agent=$agent|s$) | table _time, runtime_agent, runtime_tactic, runtime_technique, runtime_chain_stage, runtime_process, runtime_finding_id | rename runtime_agent as agent, runtime_tactic as tactic, runtime_technique as "ATT&CK", runtime_chain_stage as stage, runtime_process as process, runtime_finding_id as finding | sort - _time

panel.title: Kernel controls (Linux) — what DefenseClaw's kernel controls did

html.p: Managed Linux hosts only, and only when the enterprise Tetragon mode is observe or enforce. A control in monitor mode counts; in enforce mode it refuses the access with EPERM. A user enters the enforcing scope after a per-user burn-in with no would-block hits.

search.query: `defenseclaw_demo_kernel_denials` | stats count as denials
`defenseclaw_demo_ai_runtime_events` | where event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" AND runtime_plane="c" | stats sum(runtime_kernel_would_block_delta) as would_block

panel.title: Agent activity with no hook decision

search.query: `defenseclaw_demo_ai_runtime_events` | where event_name="ai.runtime.activity" AND runtime_hook_seen IN ("false","False") | stats count as no_hook_decision
`defenseclaw_demo_ai_runtime_events` | where event_name="ai.runtime.kernel_policy" AND runtime_kernel_event IN ("paused","operator_override") | stats dc(host) as hosts
`defenseclaw_demo_kernel_denials` | timechart span=10m count by runtime_kernel_control
`defenseclaw_demo_ai_runtime_events` | where event_name="ai.runtime.activity" AND runtime_kernel_outcome="would_block" | timechart span=10m count by runtime_kernel_control

html.p: State changes of the policies the sensor helper loaded into the host's Tetragon, by family, mode and state. One record per change, never one per kernel event.

search.query: `defenseclaw_demo_ai_runtime_events` | where event_name="ai.runtime.kernel_policy" AND runtime_kernel_policy!="" | stats count as times, latest(_time) as last_change by host, runtime_kernel_policy, runtime_kernel_family, runtime_kernel_mode, runtime_kernel_state, runtime_kernel_event | eval last_change=strftime(last_change, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") | rename runtime_kernel_policy as policy, runtime_kernel_family as family, runtime_kernel_mode as mode, runtime_kernel_state as state, runtime_kernel_event as change | sort - last_change

html.p: Covered agent hours with the event stream lossless, out of the hours burn_in needs (uid_progress every six hours; uid_ready and uid_burnin when the state changes). A would-block hit restarts the count. Covered time is agent use, not wall-clock time: 168h is about five to six working weeks for a full-time user.

search.query: `defenseclaw_demo_ai_runtime_events` | where event_name="ai.runtime.kernel_policy" AND runtime_kernel_event IN ("uid_progress","uid_ready","uid_burnin") | stats latest(runtime_kernel_event) as state, latest(runtime_kernel_covered_hours) as covered_hours, latest(runtime_kernel_needed_hours) as needed_hours, latest(runtime_kernel_reason) as reason, latest(_time) as last_change by host, runtime_user | eval progress=if(needed_hours>0, round(100*covered_hours/needed_hours, 1)."%", "") | eval last_change=strftime(last_change, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") | rename runtime_user as "user (uid)" | sort host "user (uid)"

panel.title: Kernel denials — one record per refused access

html.p: The process and the file, relative to the user's home, travel in content fields: each destination's redaction profile decides whether they leave the host. The command line is never exported. The rule is the guardrail rule the control mirrors, so a denial joins the hook record of the same intent.

search.query: `defenseclaw_demo_kernel_denials` | table _time, host, connector, runtime_user, runtime_process, runtime_kernel_target, runtime_kernel_control, runtime_kernel_rule, runtime_kernel_policy | rename runtime_user as "user (uid)", runtime_process as process, runtime_kernel_target as target, runtime_kernel_control as control, runtime_kernel_rule as rule, runtime_kernel_policy as policy | sort - _time

panel.title: Your Tetragon policies: events from AI agents

html.p: Events of the organization's own Tetragon policies (kprobe and LSM) whose process runs below an AI agent, attributed to the agent, the user and the managed hook decision of the tool call. DefenseClaw reads these events and never adds, changes or deletes the policies. Events outside an AI agent's process tree are counted on the sensor helper, never exported one by one.

search.query: `defenseclaw_demo_kernel_events` | stats sum(runtime_kernel_count) as agent_events
`defenseclaw_demo_kernel_events` | where runtime_kernel_outcome="blocked" | stats sum(runtime_kernel_count) as blocked
`defenseclaw_demo_ai_runtime_events` | where event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" AND runtime_plane="c" | stats sum(runtime_kernel_customer_events_delta) as events

panel.title: Policy, agent, action, outcome and hook join

search.query: `defenseclaw_demo_kernel_events` | stats sum(runtime_kernel_count) as events by runtime_kernel_policy_name, runtime_agent, runtime_kernel_action, runtime_kernel_outcome, runtime_hook_join | rename runtime_kernel_policy_name as policy, runtime_agent as agent, runtime_kernel_action as action, runtime_kernel_outcome as outcome, runtime_hook_join as "hook join" | sort - events

panel.title: Events of your Tetragon policies from AI agents

html.p: The target (a path or a peer) is a content field: each destination's redaction profile decides whether it leaves the host.

search.query: `defenseclaw_demo_kernel_events` | table _time, host, runtime_kernel_policy_name, runtime_kernel_hook_type, runtime_kernel_function, runtime_kernel_action, runtime_kernel_policy_mode, runtime_kernel_outcome, runtime_kernel_target, runtime_kernel_count, runtime_agent, runtime_process, runtime_user, runtime_hook_join, runtime_hook_action | rename runtime_kernel_policy_name as policy, runtime_kernel_hook_type as hook, runtime_kernel_function as function, runtime_kernel_action as action, runtime_kernel_policy_mode as mode, runtime_kernel_outcome as outcome, runtime_kernel_target as target, runtime_kernel_count as count, runtime_agent as agent, runtime_process as process, runtime_user as "user (uid)", runtime_hook_join as "hook join", runtime_hook_action as "hook action" | sort - _time
